spec.title: MeteoCore
spec.description: MeteoCore OGC server. Overview first: collection health, traffic, errors, latency, render pressure and caches at a glance. Then a tab per question: requests, rendering and caches, memory, storage and sources, one sub-tab per engine, and logs. Sections stay open; panel descriptions say what each signal means and what bad looks like. Needs Grafana 13 or newer (dashboard schema v2).

spec.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
spec.label: Prometheus
spec.description: Prometheus datasource of every metrics panel. Kept in the dashboard controls menu: the stack provisions one.

spec.name: DS_LOKI
spec.label: Loki
spec.description: Loki datasource of the log panels and the reload annotations. Kept in the dashboard controls menu: the stack provisions one.

spec.name: job
spec.label: Job
spec.description: Prometheus job scraping MeteoCore; every query is scoped to it so a shared Prometheus cannot mix in another service's http_* or process_* series.

spec.name: collection
spec.label: Collection
spec.description: Collections that report any per-collection series. Filters the per-collection panels; global ones are unaffected.

spec.name: api
spec.label: API
spec.description: The API label of the HTTP and render metrics (edr, features, maps, tiles, wms, 3dtiles, ...).

spec.name: cache
spec.label: Cache
spec.description: Byte-bounded caches, discovered from every `<name>_cache_hits_total` family the server exposes; drives the cache table and the repeated per-cache cards.

spec.title: Collections
spec.description: Collections by /health state now. Ready serve normally. Degraded serve with reduced capability: database unreachable, empty catalog, a truncated station list, a broker session down. Failed could not be built; a reload or the background retry may bring them back. Degraded and failed should be 0: /health names the reason and the Warnings & errors log says why.

spec.title: Requests/s
spec.description: HTTP requests per second over the last 5 min, for the APIs picked in API.

spec.title: 5xx ratio
spec.description: Share of responses with a 5xx status over the last 5 min, 503 load shedding included. Amber from 0.5 %, red from 2 %. Any sustained value is worth a look at the error log.

spec.expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5.."}[5m])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[5m]))

spec.title: Latency p95
spec.description: 95th percentile HTTP latency over the last 5 min across the picked APIs (health and metrics excluded). Amber from 1 s, red from 3 s. Quantiles are unreliable below ~0.1 req/s; p50 and p99 are in Requests & latency.

spec.title: Render queue
spec.description: Requests waiting for raster memory or a render slot, as a share of the queue capacity. Amber from 5 %, red from 50 %; a full queue answers 503 at once.

spec.title: Cache hit ratio
spec.description: Hits as a share of all lookups over the last 5 min, summed over every byte-bounded cache, so the busiest caches weigh most. Red below 30 %, amber below 60 %; no data, in grey, means no cache had a lookup in the window. It dips after a restart while caches refill; a lasting drop means the working set no longer fits. The All caches table has each cache.

spec.title: Requests by API
spec.description: Requests per second by API, stacked. A sudden change of shape usually means a client changed its configuration, not that the server did.

spec.title: Latency p95 by API
spec.description: p95 per API. Dashed lines mark 1 s and 3 s. Quantiles are unreliable below ~0.1 req/s: they interpolate to bucket tops from single samples, so check the request rate before believing a spike on a quiet API. A gap is a minute with no requests: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", api!=""}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Errors & shedding
spec.description: 4xx = client mistakes (bad parameters, unknown collections). 5xx = server faults, read the error log. 503 = load shed by render, decode or read admission; it is part of 5xx in the ratio stat but drawn on its own here.

spec.expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5..", status!="503"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

spec.title: Render pressure
spec.description: Share of the render executor in use: render slots busy (`[server] render_concurrency`), the admission queue filled, and the render memory budget reserved (MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB). Dashed lines mark 70 % and 90 %. Brief peaks are normal during animation; lines that stay high mean renders wait, and a full queue or budget answers 503.

spec.title: Requests by route — top 10
spec.description: The ten busiest route templates per step, for the picked APIs.

spec.title: Errors by status code
spec.description: 4xx and 5xx responses per second by status code, stacked: 4xx in amber shades, 5xx in red shades, 503 shedding in purple.

spec.title: Routes
spec.description: Every route template over the dashboard's time range, for the picked APIs: requests, the share answered 4xx and 5xx, p95 and p99 latency, and bytes served. 5xx is amber from 0.1 % and red from 1 %; latency amber from 1 s and red from 3 s. Sort by any column.

spec.expr: (sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"4.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))) / sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))

(sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))) / sum by (path, api) (increase(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, path, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, path, api) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__range])))

spec.title: Latency p50 · p95 · p99
spec.description: Request latency across the picked APIs. Pick API = wms for the WMS view: GetMap, GetCapabilities and GetFeatureInfo share the /wms route, so p50 is mostly warm hits and the p99 tail cold renders. The render alone, by outcome and collection, is in Rendering & admission. A gap is a minute with no requests: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: Latency p95 by route — top 10
spec.description: The ten slowest route templates per step, among routes serving at least 0.01 req/s (quieter routes only produce noise). A gap is a minute with no requests: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, path) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", api!=""}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (path) (sum by (path) (rate(http_requests_total{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0.01))

spec.title: Egress
spec.description: Response bytes per second over the last 5 min, for the picked APIs.

spec.title: Egress by API
spec.description: Response bytes per second by API, stacked. Responses without a known length are not counted (no handler streams).

spec.title: Served by API
spec.description: Bytes served per API over the dashboard's time range.

spec.title: EDR queries — rate by route
spec.description: EDR data routes only (position, area, radius, cube, trajectory, locations; metadata routes excluded): radar probes and point queries, lightning windows, station time series, vertical cross-sections.

spec.title: EDR queries — p95 by route
spec.description: p95 per EDR data route. A PVOL position resamples polar volumes (tens of ms warm, seconds after a remote fetch); a lightning area is one indexed SQL window (ms). A route drifting up under steady traffic is an engine or database regression, not client load. A gap is a minute with no EDR queries: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: EDR queries — 4xx · 5xx by route
spec.description: 4xx on area routes includes the response-size budget (QueryTooLarge 400): usually a client widening its area, parameters or time window. Any 5xx is ours: read the logs.

spec.title: Render slots busy
spec.description: Render slots in use of `[server] render_concurrency`, shared by WMS, Maps, Tiles and 3D Tiles. Brief peaks are normal during animation; sitting at the top means renders queue.

spec.title: Render memory reserved
spec.description: Share of the transient raster render budget (MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB) reserved by renders in flight.

spec.title: Cold renders/s
spec.description: WMS, Maps and Tiles renders that had to read source data (render outcome `cold`) over the last 5 min, for the picked APIs and collections. This is the render cost that drives the latency tail.

spec.title: 503 shed /1h
spec.description: 503 responses in the last hour: requests turned away by render, decode or read admission (queue full, memory budget, deadline). Clients retry these, so a few are harmless; a steady stream means the server is short of render slots or memory.

spec.title: Render slots
spec.description: Slots in use against `[server] render_concurrency` (default 2× CPUs, min 8; fixed at boot). Flat at the top = renders queueing; brief touches are normal during animation bursts.

spec.title: Render queue
spec.description: Requests waiting for raster memory or a render slot, against MC_RENDER_QUEUE_CAPACITY (default 3× render concurrency). A full queue answers 503 at once.

spec.title: Render memory
spec.description: Transient output-buffer estimate (32 bytes per output pixel; composites add a plane per band) reserved by renders in flight, against MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB. Separate from source decoding and resident caches.

spec.title: Shedding & deadlines
spec.description: Raster renders refused with 503 by the shared render executor, per minute. At once: queue full, or oversize (larger than the whole memory budget). Deadline by stage: queue = expired waiting for memory or a slot, render = expired after admission. `memory wait expired` is the part of the queue deadlines spent waiting for memory (dashed: already counted).

spec.title: Cold renders & meta-tile declines
spec.description: Render work per second. Meta-tiles rendered = meta-tile cache misses (decode + resample + colorize), the cost signal p99 spikes track. Declined = WMS views whose covering tile count exceeded the pixel-proportional budget and fell back to an uncached direct render; a sustained rate means clients send viewports outside the cacheable envelope. Cold renders = requests whose render read source data.

spec.title: Render latency by outcome
spec.description: WMS GetMap, Maps map and Tiles map-tile render latency, from the rendered-cache lookup to the response, for the picked APIs and collections; p95 solid, p99 dashed. hit = rendered-cache hit (sub-ms), assembled = WMS view built from cached meta-tiles, cold = the engine read source data: the render a user actually waits for. Shed and expired renders are not here: see Shedding & deadlines. A gap is a minute with no renders: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: Render p95 by collection — top 10
spec.description: Which collection owns the render tail (cold and assembled; hits are sub-ms everywhere). One slow collection with the others flat points at its source (remote store, decode, overview choice), not at render admission. Click a series to filter the dashboard to it. A gap is a minute with no renders: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, collection, outcome) (rate(render_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api", collection=~"$collection", outcome!="hit"}[$__rate_interval]))))

spec.title: Render phases — p50
spec.description: Where a typical served render spends its time, by API and phase. queue = waiting for raster memory and a render slot; engine = get_raster_tile (source read, decode, reproject; summed over a WMS view's uncached meta-tiles); assemble = WMS meta-tile resample; encode = colorize + image encode. Hits run no phase. Phases carry no collection label, so the collection picker does not apply. A gap is a minute with no renders: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, api, phase) (rate(render_phase_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Render phases — p95
spec.description: Where the slow renders spend their time. A rising queue line over a flat engine line means too few render slots (`[server] render_concurrency`); a rising engine line means a slow source. Expired renders are not here: see the stage split in Shedding & deadlines. A gap is a minute with no renders: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, api, phase) (rate(render_phase_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", api=~"$api"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.title: Slow renders (> 0.5 s)
spec.description: Every slow WMS render log line, for the picked collections: layer, render time, time waiting for a slot (sem_wait), tiles and misses of a meta-tiled view, size, and the render path.

spec.expr: {job="meteocore"} |~ "slow WMS (meta-tile |direct )?render" | json | layer=~"($collection)(/.*)?" | line_format "{{.layer}}  {{.render_ms}} ms  sem_wait={{.sem_wait_ms}} ms  tiles={{.tiles}} misses={{.misses}}  {{.width}}x{{.height}}  ({{.message}})"

spec.title: All caches
spec.description: One row per byte-bounded cache picked in Cache, over the dashboard's time range: hit ratio, misses per second (misses are work: decodes, renders, remote fetches), fill against the configured capacity, resident bytes and entries where the cache counts them. An LRU is meant to fill; 100 % is only a sizing signal when the hit ratio sags with it and misses rise. Per-collection caches follow the Collection picker; global caches always show. New `<name>_cache_*` families appear here without a dashboard change.

spec.expr: sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) / ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__range:1m]))) > 0)

spec.title: Misses by cache — top 8
spec.description: Misses per second for the eight busiest caches: actual work (decodes, renders, remote fetches). A cache whose misses jump while traffic is flat is churning, not loaded.

spec.title: Fill by cache
spec.description: Resident bytes as a share of each cache's configured capacity.

spec.title: ${cache}
spec.description: One card per cache picked in Cache (repeated): hit ratio and fill on the left axis, misses per second on the right. Healthy: a steady hit ratio. Fill pinned at 100 % is fine while the hit ratio holds; 100 % with a sagging ratio and rising misses means the working set no longer fits. No line = no lookups in the window. A gap is a minute with no lookups: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: Resident set size of the server process. Off Linux, where RSS is not read, this shows jemalloc resident bytes instead.

spec.title: Allocator overhead
spec.description: jemalloc resident ÷ allocated: physical pages held per byte the application uses. Healthy below 1.5×; the glibc fragmentation incident ran at ~3×.

spec.title: Process memory
spec.description: Healthy: RSS ≈ jemalloc resident, and resident within ~1.5× of allocated (live application bytes). resident ≫ allocated = allocator retention or fragmentation; resident ≫ active = freed pages awaiting purge, which jemalloc's background threads return over its 10 s decay. RSS ≫ jemalloc resident = memory outside the allocator (mapped files, thread stacks). Swap > 0 = host memory pressure. `caches` is the sum of every byte-bounded cache, the floor the process cannot go below. RSS and swap are read on Linux only. jemalloc retained is address space, not memory: see Retained address space.

spec.title: Retained address space
spec.description: Virtual memory jemalloc keeps mapped for reuse instead of unmapping it (jemalloc_retained_bytes). It is address space, not memory: its pages were purged or never touched, so it is not part of RSS, and tens of GiB are normal on a 64-bit host. Worth a look only when it keeps growing while allocated stays flat in Process memory, a sign of arena fragmentation.

spec.title: Memory now
spec.description: A snapshot of the same accounting: RSS, allocator resident and live allocations, the bytes held by caches, and the transient bytes admission budgets have reserved.

spec.title: Cache memory by cache
spec.description: Resident bytes per cache, stacked: where the cache part of RSS goes.

spec.title: Admission budgets — use
spec.description: Transient memory reserved against each admission budget: render (MC_RENDER_MEMORY_MB), GeoTIFF decode (MC_GEOTIFF_DECODE_MEMORY_MB), Zarr read (MC_ZARR_READ_MEMORY_MB), NetCDF field read (MC_NETCDF_READ_MEMORY_MB), station-grid compute (MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB), EDR response bodies (MC_EDR_RESPONSE_MEMORY_MB), PVOL EDR reads (MC_PVOL_READ_MEMORY_MB). These are admission estimates, not measured RSS; a request that does not fit is answered 503.

spec.title: Admission rejections
spec.description: Requests turned away (503) per minute by each memory budget. Admission fails at once rather than waiting while it holds a render slot, except render memory, which waits in the render queue until its deadline.

spec.title: Admission budgets
spec.description: Each budget's reserved bytes now, its capacity, the use, the most it held at once over the dashboard's time range (Peak, from *_reserved_peak_bytes), and requests it rejected over the dashboard's time range (oversize and expired memory waits for render).

spec.expr: label_replace(sum(increase(geotiff_decode_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "geotiff_decode", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(zarr_read_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "zarr_read", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(netcdf_read_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "netcdf_read", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(station_grid_compute_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "station_grid_compute", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(edr_response_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "edr_response", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(pvol_read_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "pvol_read", "", "") or label_replace(sum(increase(render_budget_rejected_total{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "render", "", "")

label_replace(max(max_over_time(geotiff_decode_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "geotiff_decode", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(zarr_read_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "zarr_read", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(netcdf_read_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "netcdf_read", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(station_grid_compute_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "station_grid_compute", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(edr_response_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "edr_response", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(pvol_read_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "pvol_read", "", "") or label_replace(max(max_over_time(render_budget_reserved_peak_bytes{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "budget", "render", "", "")

spec.title: Stale feeds
spec.description: Collections whose newest data is older than 1.5 times their own peak age of the day before, and older than 15 min. Data age is a sawtooth with each feed's cadence, so a fixed threshold cannot fit a radar and a model run; yesterday's peak can. Collections younger than a day are not counted. Also counted: collections that hold no data at all (collection_has_data 0), which have no data age: one that never loaded any, or whose data all aged out of its window.

spec.expr: (count((max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) > 1.5 * max by (collection) (max_over_time(collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1d] offset 1d))) > 900) or vector(0)) + (count(max by (collection) (collection_has_data{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) == 0) or vector(0))

spec.title: Collections by state
spec.description: Configured collections and how many were ready, degraded or failed over time: when did a collection stop being ready, and did a reload bring it back? Ready + degraded + failed = configured. The Collections stat on Overview is the latest point.

spec.title: Freshness
spec.description: Each collection's data age now, its peak age the day before, and the ratio. Data age climbs between deliveries and drops when new data lands, so a ratio well above 1 means the feed has stalled while the collection still reports ready. Amber from 1.5, red from 3; the Stale feeds stat counts the amber ones older than 15 min.

spec.expr: max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) / max by (collection) (max_over_time(collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1d] offset 1d))

spec.title: Data age by collection
spec.description: Seconds since the newest data each collection serves (/health data_age_secs): GeoTIFF newest timestep, QueryData and NetCDF newest run, BUFR newest report, satellite newest scan, nowcast anchor frame. A sawtooth with the feed's cadence is normal. Bad: a line climbing past its usual peak. Negative = the newest data lies in the future. Click a series to filter the dashboard to it. A collection holding no data has no line; the Stale feeds stat counts it.

spec.title: Remote reads
spec.description: Bytes per second read from S3/HTTP sources over the last 5 min, for the picked collections. Local-file collections read ~0.

spec.title: Remote reads by collection
spec.description: Bytes per second fetched from S3/HTTP sources (cold COG tiles, PVOL volumes, GRIB messages, NetCDF chunks). A burst on a PVOL collection is pixel-cache misses being fetched again (Engines › Radar).

spec.title: Remote requests per host
spec.description: Requests to each rate-limited remote host (today the remote NetCDF sources): in flight, waiting for a permit, and the host's limit (dashed). Polls take at most 2 permits. A queue that stays up means requests wait on the host, and that wait counts against their deadline.

spec.title: Fetched by engine
spec.description: Bytes read from remote storage per engine type over the dashboard's time range.

spec.title: Fetched by collection — top 10
spec.description: Bytes read from remote storage per collection over the dashboard's time range.

spec.title: PVOL pixel cache — churn
spec.description: The pre-warm keeps every advertised timestep's lowest prewarm_sweeps sweeps of the default quantity (or of prewarm_quantities) resident, if it fits. Sustained inserts while entries sit flat at capacity = churn: pre-warmed frames are evicted and the next animation pays burst re-reads from storage. Fix: raise MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB to about twice the working set (sites × window ÷ cadence × prewarm_sweeps × pre-warmed quantities × one sweep). Read failures = moments that degraded to nodata (missing file, decode failure). Aborted reads = reads that failed their request instead, by reason: deadline (cut off by the request deadline; the read is finished in the background for the retry) or storage (a failure a retry can heal, or a 401/403 refusal).

spec.title: PVOL pixel cache — resident
spec.description: Resident bytes against MC_PVOL_PIXEL_CACHE_MB, and the entry count (right axis).

spec.title: Radar & 3D caches — hit ratio
spec.description: ODIM composite (full HDF5 decodes), PVOL pixel, voxel-grid (polar resamples for 3D meshes), storm-cell set (segmentations) and 3D Tiles encoded-content caches. A gap is a minute with no lookups: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: Radar & 3D caches — fill
spec.description: Resident bytes as a share of each cache's capacity.

spec.title: Lead-1 skill vs persistence
spec.description: Realized 5-min skill: each generation scores the previous one's lead-1 prediction against the fresh analysis (CSI), next to the persistence baseline (dashed). The nowcast must sit above its baseline; a collapsing gap = motion or source-data regression.

spec.title: Generation duration
spec.description: Wall-clock of the newest generation. It must stay well under the source cadence (300 s for a 5-min composite, the red line); above it, generations queue and the served time axis lags reality.

spec.title: Generations & failures per hour
spec.description: Generations in the trailing hour: ~12 at a 5-min source cadence; dips = skipped source frames. Any failure deserves a log read (the engine serves the previous generation meanwhile).

spec.title: Source lag
spec.description: Age of the source anchor frame when the generation finished: upstream latency plus generation time. Sustained growth = the source stalled, and every future frame goes stale with it.

spec.title: Retention
spec.description: Retained generations (the reference-time pinning window; resident memory multiplies with it) and frames (analysis + leads) in the newest generation.

spec.title: Cell tracker per hour
spec.description: Association bookkeeping in the trailing hour. Births and deaths above real cell turnover mean dropouts; pass-2 matches are the raw-position fallback (see the share); velocity clamps are jumps the tracker already rejected as motion. On quiet weather all sit at zero.

spec.title: Pass-2 share of matches
spec.description: pass-2 ÷ (pass-1 + pass-2) over the trailing hour. Pass 2 rescues counter-flow cells and also completes identity swaps; a rising share with steady cell counts is the first sign of swaps between co-located echoes. Empty when nothing matched.

spec.expr: sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass2_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h])) / ((sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass1_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h])) + sum by (collection) (increase(nowcast_cell_pass2_matches_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[1h]))) > 0)

spec.title: Per-collection caches
spec.description: Caches kept per collection, over the dashboard's time range: GeoTIFF compressed tiles (tile_cache), GRIB decoded grids (grid_cache) and compressed messages (grib_message_cache; its hits measure reuse after grid misses, and its misses need storage reads) and point indexes of CCSDS and complex-packed messages (grib_point_index_cache; a miss is one decode of a message a position query reads for the first time), Zarr decoded chunks (zarr_decoded_cache; single-flight waiters count as hits), a plain Zarr store's objects (zarr_object_cache) and the compressed chunk ranges an Icechunk repository reads (zarr_icechunk_payload_cache; its misses are storage requests). GRIB budgets are per source: grid_cache_mb, message_cache_mb and point_index_cache_mb.

spec.expr: sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_object_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) / ((sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_object_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__range:1m])) + sum by (cache, collection) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_object_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_misses_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__range:1m]))) > 0)

sum by (cache, collection) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_object_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_bytes", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_bytes")) / (sum by (cache, collection) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_object_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_capacity_bytes", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_capacity_bytes")) > 0)

spec.title: Per-collection cache hit ratio
spec.description: Hit ratio per cache and collection. A ratio sagging while the cache's fill stays at 100 % means the working set no longer fits its per-source budget. A gap is a minute with no lookups: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.expr: topk(12, sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) / ((sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_hits_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) + sum by (cache, collection) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(tile_cache|grid_cache|grib_message_cache|grib_point_index_cache|zarr_decoded_cache|zarr_icechunk_payload_cache)_misses_total", collection=~"$collection"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__rate_interval:15s]))) > 0))

spec.title: Per-collection cache misses
spec.description: Misses per second per cache and collection: decodes (grid, Zarr chunk, GRIB point index) and storage reads (GeoTIFF tile, GRIB message, Icechunk chunk range).

spec.title: NetCDF detached field fills
spec.description: Cold remote NetCDF fields are fetched by a task the request hands its fill to; it finishes after the request's deadline and leaves the field cached. Pending = running now (at most 16). Inline = fills a request ran itself because 16 were running; a steady inline rate means fetches cannot keep up with the frames asked for. EDR and GetFeatureInfo reads use a pool of their own and are not counted.

spec.title: Per-collection cache memory
spec.description: Resident bytes per cache and collection, stacked.

spec.title: Scan windows vs scan cache
spec.description: Bytes of the scans in each satellite collection's time window, the part held in memory, and MC_SATELLITE_FRAME_CACHE_MB (dashed). Bad: all windows above capacity (the poll logs a WARN and stops downloading back), or resident below window for more than a poll or two: requests then download scans within the render deadline, and an animation's older frames answer 503.

spec.title: Scan downloads per hour
spec.description: Scans downloaded again by a poll after the scan cache evicted them, and scans a request had to download (scan-cache misses), in the trailing hour. Once the windows fit, request fetches stay near 0; a steady re-download rate means the windows barely fit.

spec.title: Stations behind the latest analysis
spec.description: Stations the latest analysis of each station-grid parameter was computed from: the first thing to check when an analysis looks wrong. A drop means the source lost stations and the field is interpolated from fewer, farther ones; 0 draws an empty map. Dashed: the stations with a leave-one-out residual, those with another station within the search radius; the gap to the solid line is the isolated stations.

spec.title: Analyses, failures & duration
spec.description: Analyses in the trailing hour (request misses plus the poll's pre-compute and revisions), failed analyses and source reads, analyses rejected (503) because MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB was full, and the last analysis's duration (right axis). A duration near the 3 s render deadline means cold map requests answer 503 until the pre-compute catches up.

spec.title: Station-grid cache
spec.description: Hit ratio of the shared analysis cache and its fill against MC_STATION_GRID_CACHE_MB. Every revision of the observations re-keys a collection's grids, so a burst of misses after a late report is expected; a low ratio otherwise means the cache holds fewer grids than the maps animate over. A gap is a minute with no lookups: the traffic comes in bursts with the 5-minute radar cadence.

spec.title: Computation admission
spec.description: Bytes reserved by analyses being computed, against MC_STATION_GRID_MEMORY_MB (dashed).

spec.title: Leave-one-out RMSE
spec.description: Root mean square of the leave-one-out residuals of the latest analysis of each station-grid parameter, in the parameter's own units: at every station, the analysis from the other stations minus the station's value. It measures how well the method fits the network. A step up means a station reports values its neighbours do not support (a faulty sensor, a wrong position) or the network thinned. Find the station with the collection's Features items sorted by residual (sortby=-residual, then sortby=residual).

spec.title: Database reachable
spec.description: Per collection, the latest 30 s SELECT 1 ping. Down = the collection is degraded in /health. Click a row to filter the dashboard to it.

spec.title: Collections down
spec.description: PostGIS collections whose latest ping failed.

spec.title: Truncated lists
spec.description: Collections whose cached station list was cut at `[postgis] max_locations`: stations past the cap are missing from /locations, Features and, in the observation-derived modes, from position and area. In mode B a cut station registry counts too. /health shows them degraded. Should be 0: raise max_locations or narrow the station set.

spec.title: Connection pool
spec.description: Per pool: open connections against capacity (dashed), connections acquirable now, and tasks waiting (amber). Sustained waiting > 0 = pool too small or slow queries.

spec.title: Pings & metadata refreshes
spec.description: In the trailing hour: failed pings (flip /health) and failed metadata refreshes (the previous snapshot is kept, so locations go stale), next to the totals so a flat zero failure line is not mistaken for nothing running. Right axis: the slowest last metadata refresh.

spec.title: Broker session
spec.description: Per collection: connected and subscribed to the WIS2 Global Broker, or reconnecting. /health degrades after degrade_after_secs. Click a row to filter the dashboard to it.

spec.title: Notification age & lag
spec.description: Age = seconds since the last accepted notification; it climbs between publications (MeteoAlarm is sporadic, SYNOP bursts at H+20). Lag = receipt − pubtime of the last one: seconds normally; a growing lag means the broker is replaying a backlog after a reconnect.

spec.title: Notifications per minute
spec.description: Accepted vs dropped by reason. Every notification is republished once per Global Cache, so dropped·duplicate ≈ 5× accepted is the healthy shape. Any other reason growing is a problem: parse = non-WNM payloads, policy = a link failed the download policy, integrity = checksum mismatch, size = over max_download_bytes, download = HTTP failures, decode = bad inline payload.

spec.expr: sum by (collection) (rate(wis2_messages_received_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[5m]) * 60) - sum by (collection) (rate(wis2_messages_dropped_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[5m]) * 60)

spec.title: Downloads, reconnects & unverified
spec.description: In the trailing hour. Downloads are needed only for link-only notifications (most SYNOP arrives inline). Reconnects should be rare; a steady rate means the broker keeps closing the session (keep-alive, session expiry, client id collisions). Unverified = sha3-* checksums accepted without checking.

spec.title: CAP alerts
spec.description: active = alert areas in the served catalog after Update/Cancel resolution (every source mode); held = alerts in the WIS2 accumulator. Right axis, trailing hour: superseded by a reference chain; evicted = expired past retention_grace or over max_alerts; evicted valid = still-valid alerts the max_alerts cap pushed out (should be 0).

spec.title: CAP over WIS2 — documents & geometry hints
spec.description: In the trailing hour. Documents: ingested, rejected (unparseable XML: a producer problem), deleted. Geometry hints (MeteoAlarm rel=geometry zone polygons): attached, or rejected (link expired, not a polygon, outside the notification bbox). A rising rejected share means alerts render without geometry.

spec.title: BUFR store
spec.description: Stations and reports held after pruning (retention × max_stations); reports on the right axis. A global SYNOP subscription levels off around 20 k stations × 24 hourly rows; a step down is a prune or a rebuild on reload. Flat at 0 with a ready collection = the source is empty or every report is out of the window.

spec.title: BUFR ingest per hour
spec.description: In the trailing hour: files or payloads fetched; reports ingested (new station-time rows), replaced (corrections), out_of_window (clock skew or a stale feed), skipped (no station id, position or time), nil (NIL bulletins: a centre with no report to send, not a failure); decode failures by kind (error = malformed BUFR, unsupported = a decoder gap: a steady rate from one centre means its template needs the decoder extended); failed source scans.

spec.title: Requests by API & query type
spec.description: From the request logs: requests per second by API and query type (both Loki labels). Health and metrics requests carry no API and are left out.

spec.title: Error responses by status class
spec.description: From the request logs: 4xx and 5xx responses per second.

spec.title: Requests by collection — top 10
spec.description: From the request logs, which carry the collection id that the HTTP metrics deliberately do not: the ten busiest collections. Parses every request line, so wide time ranges are slow.

spec.expr: topk(10, sum by (collection) (rate({job="meteocore", api=~"$api", api!=""} | json collection="collection" | collection!="" | collection=~"$collection" [$__auto])))

spec.title: Warnings & errors
spec.description: WARN and ERROR events (not request lines): failed or degraded collections, reload problems, poll and source errors. With collections picked, only lines naming one of them.

spec.title: Error responses
spec.description: Request log lines answered 4xx or 5xx, with the error reason the API attached.

spec.expr: {job="meteocore", status_class=~"4xx|5xx", api=~"$api"} | json | collection=~"$collection" | line_format "{{.method}} {{.path}} → {{.status}} ({{.duration_ms}} ms) {{.error}} {{if .query}}?{{.query}}{{end}}"

spec.title: Recent requests
spec.description: All request log lines, newest first. Expand a line for every field; request_id matches the X-Request-ID response header.

spec.expr: {job="meteocore", api=~"$api"} | json | collection=~"$collection" | line_format "{{.method}} {{.path}} → {{.status}} ({{.duration_ms}} ms) rid={{.request_id}} {{if .query}}?{{.query}}{{end}}"

spec.title: GRIB point fields by path
spec.description: Position-query fields read per second per GRIB source, by how: partial reads only the CCSDS blocks (ECMWF) or complex-packed rows (GFS) the points need through the point index, full samples a decoded grid. Fields read in full mean point_index_cache_mb = 0, a window the grid cache keeps without a message cache, a first read of each parameter, or a packing or layout the point index does not read.

spec.title: GRIB point fetches by mode
spec.description: GETs per second GRIB position queries make, by mode: whole messages, prefixes of messages not yet indexed, ranges of the indexed blocks or rows a query needs, and continuations of a prefix or range that came up short. Partial modes run without a message cache, or for a window it cannot hold; a steady continuation rate means prefix predictions run short.

spec.title: GRIB point fetch bytes by mode
spec.description: Bytes per second GRIB position queries fetch, by mode, as in GRIB point fetches by mode. Whole messages are 0.3 to 1.4 MB each for ECMWF fields; a range is a few kilobytes, a prefix as much of the message as the points' southernmost row needs.

spec.title: 429 answers per host
spec.description: 429 Too Many Requests answers from each rate-limited remote host (today the remote NetCDF sources), per second, to every store and collection on it. Each one spaces the host's requests apart and can halve its request limit (the panel above), and the request it refused is retried after 2 s. Zero is normal. A rate that stays up means the host is refusing work: polls open a few files each and catch up over several, and requests to the host wait their turn against their deadline.

spec.title: Retryable answers by collection
spec.description: Answers from remote hosts that object_store retries, per second, by the collection whose request got one, the host and the status: a 5xx (an S3 bucket's 503 SlowDown), 429 or 408. Every attempt counts, retries included, and each retry waits a back-off first (0.1 s, doubling), so a rate that stays up is time added to polls and cold queries. Zero is normal. A blank collection is a store no engine named.

spec.title: Cache plan
spec.description: Every cache and admission budget with where its size came from: default, env:<variable>, config:<[server] key>, collection:<collection key> or constant (/admin/cache-plan has the same list). Capacity is the configured size and Used what the cache holds or the budget has reserved now. A cache without a byte gauge yet (MVT, solid images, plain-Zarr objects) shows no Used. Demand is what the engines say the cache must hold for their data (cache_demand_bytes; a floor for PVOL pixels), empty for a cache without one; /admin/cache-plan has its inputs and the suggested size. Planned is the size the memory plan gives each one (cache_planned_bytes), fitted at boot and at each reload to the plan's total; 0 for a cache no collection can reach. A report: the configured size is unchanged. /admin/cache-plan says why each size.

spec.expr: max by (cache, collection) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~".+_cache_bytes"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_bytes")) or max by (cache) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~".+_reserved_bytes"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_reserved_bytes")) or label_replace(max(render_budget_total_bytes{job=~"$job"}) - max(render_budget_available_bytes{job=~"$job"}), "cache", "render_budget", "", "")

spec.title: Configured capacity
spec.description: Configured capacity of every cache and of every admission budget, summed (memory_capacity_total_bytes). Capacity, not memory: a cache holds no more than it is asked for, and budgets are reserved only while work runs. The Cache plan table lists each one, with the size the memory plan gives it; Memory plan has the plan's total.

spec.title: Memory outside caches
spec.description: RSS less every *_cache_bytes, stacked by where it is: stores = the in-memory stores that report their size (BUFR reports and snapshot, the WIS2 dedup and BUFR deletion indexes, CAP alerts, nowcast frames, PVOL catalogs, NetCDF open files; see Store memory), heap without a gauge = jemalloc allocated less the caches and the stores, allocator slack = active less allocated (fragmentation), dirty pages = resident less active (freed pages awaiting purge), outside jemalloc = RSS less jemalloc resident (thread stacks, mapped files). A growing heap without a gauge is memory no gauge explains yet. RSS is read on Linux only, so the top band is empty elsewhere.

spec.title: Store memory
spec.description: Heap the in-memory stores hold, per collection, stacked: estimates weighed like cache entries (buffer capacities, map tables and nodes), computed when the store changes. bufr_store and bufr_snapshot follow retention and max_stations; bufr_deletion_index and wis2_dedup grow to 200000 data_ids (about 145 and 130 MB); cap is the WIS2 accumulator, the published catalog and the geocode lookup; nowcast_frame is exact, max_pixels × frames × generations × 1 or 4 bytes; pvol_catalog is parsed volume metadata; netcdf_open_file the readers' parsed metadata, modelled per file.

spec.title: Admission budgets — peak
spec.description: The most each budget held at once since the previous scrape (*_reserved_peak_bytes, taken and restarted at every scrape), as a share of its capacity: bursts between scrapes that Admission budgets — use, a sample at scrape time, misses. 1 = full; near 1 often means a raised capacity would be used. Each scrape restarts the marks, so a second scraper of the same server sees only what came after the other's scrape.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since the server process started (process_start_time_seconds). Read cumulative counters against it: a cache with few lookups in a short uptime has had no demand yet.

spec.title: Heap without a gauge
spec.description: jemalloc allocated less every cache and every store that reports its size: heap no gauge explains. Should stay flat; a steady climb is a store or leak to meter next.

spec.title: WIS2 dedup and deletion indexes
spec.description: data_ids each WIS2 subscription's duplicate filter remembers (dedup: dedup_window, PT1H by default, at most 200000), and the data_ids whose rows a BUFR collection remembers to honour rel=deletion (deletion index, at most 200000, about 5 h of a global feed). Both reach their cap on a busy subscription; their bytes are in Memory & admission › Store memory.

spec.title: Cache churn, last hour
spec.description: One row per cache family picked in Cache, over the last hour (#1308): does it need memory? Label, as /admin/cache-plan labels it: idle = under 60 lookups, so fill and hit ratio say nothing yet; thrashing = turnover above 1 and ghost hits within 1 × capacity at least 20 % of misses, so more memory helps; scan = turnover above 1 and ghost hits within 2 × under 5 % of misses, a one-pass read that a bypass fixes, not memory; churning = turnover above 1 in a cache without a ghost ring, which cannot tell: give that cache a ring (ByteBoundedCache::with_ghosts) to find out; healthy = the rest, which can lend memory. Turnover is capacities admitted per hour. Cold share is the evictions of entries never read since inserted. Ghost hits are misses of keys evicted recently, as a share of misses; with hits they give the hit ratio of a cache twice as large. Ghost columns are empty for caches without a ring: the meta-tile, rendered, GeoTIFF decoded-chunk, PVOL pixel and GRIB grid and message caches keep one. Per-collection families sum their collections; pick one in Collection to see it alone. Pre-warmed caches (PVOL pixel, GeoTIFF tiles) insert ahead of reads, so their evictions and ghost hits undervalue them. The thresholds are starting points.

spec.expr: ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) < 60) * 0 + 1 or (((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_inserted_bytes_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_inserted_bytes_total")[1h:1m])) / (sum by (cache) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_capacity_bytes", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_capacity_bytes")) > 0)) > 1) and ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="1"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) >= 0.2)) * 0 + 2 or (((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_inserted_bytes_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_inserted_bytes_total")[1h:1m])) / (sum by (cache) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_capacity_bytes", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_capacity_bytes")) > 0)) > 1) and ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="2"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) < 0.05)) * 0 + 3 or (((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_inserted_bytes_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_inserted_bytes_total")[1h:1m])) / (sum by (cache) (label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_capacity_bytes", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_capacity_bytes")) > 0)) > 1) unless (sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="1"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m])))) * 0 + 4 or (sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) * 0

sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) > 0)

sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_evictions_total", collection=~"$collection|", ring="cold"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_evictions_total")[1h:1m])) / (sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_evictions_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_evictions_total")[1h:1m])) > 0)

(sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="1"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m])))

(sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="2"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m])) / sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m])))

(sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|", depth="1"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[1h:1m]))) / ((sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[1h:1m])) + sum by (cache) (increase(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[1h:1m]))) > 0)

spec.title: Evictions by cache and ring
spec.description: Entries evicted per second (#1308). cold = never read since inserted, once the cache is full: evicted before a second use; hot = read since. Refused inserts and new values of a resident key are not evictions. Evictions alone are normal for a full cache: whether they cost hits is the ghost-hit panel's question.

spec.title: Turnover by cache
spec.description: Capacities admitted per hour: bytes inserted for keys not resident, per hour, over the configured capacity (#1308). Above 1 a cache replaces its contents within the hour: thrashing when the ghost hits say evicted keys come back, a scan when they do not.

spec.title: Ghost hits as a share of misses
spec.description: Misses of a key the cache evicted within depth × its capacity of evictions, as a share of its misses (#1308): the misses a cache 1.5, 2 or 3 times as large would have hit. At least 20 % within 1 × with turnover above 1 is thrashing; under 5 % within 2 × is a scan. Only caches with a ghost ring report.

spec.expr: sum by (cache, depth) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) / on (cache) group_left () (sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) > 0)

spec.title: Estimated hit ratio with more memory
spec.description: The hit ratio now (depth 0) and what a cache 1.5, 2 or 3 times as large would have had: hits plus the ghost hits within 0.5, 1 or 2 × its capacity, over lookups (#1308). A wide gap is memory well spent; none means a larger cache buys nothing. Only caches with a ghost ring.

spec.expr: sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) / (sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) + sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) > 0)

(sum by (cache, depth) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_ghost_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_ghost_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) + on (cache) group_left () sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s]))) / on (cache) group_left () (sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_hits_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_hits_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) + sum by (cache) (rate(label_replace({job=~"$job", __name__=~"(${cache})_misses_total", collection=~"$collection|"}, "cache", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)_misses_total")[$__rate_interval:15s])) > 0)

spec.title: Inserted and evicted bytes
spec.description: Bytes admitted for keys not resident, and bytes evicted, per second (#1308). Evictions trail inserts by a full cache while it fills; once full they match, and the inserts over the capacity are its turnover.

spec.title: Refused inserts
spec.description: Inserts a cache refused because the entry outweighs its shard's hot target, so it was never cached (#1308). Not evictions. A steady rate means entries too large for the cache's shards: a larger cache, fewer shards or a higher hot share.

spec.title: GRIB reads around the grid cache
spec.description: Field reads per second that went around the GRIB grid cache, by source: a window of more fields than it holds, read without inserting (#1297), against its misses (#1308). Bypasses are neither hits nor misses, so a meteogram's one-pass read stays out of the map workload's hit ratio.

spec.title: GRIB pre-warm: messages fetched and read
spec.description: Messages per second the GRIB pre-warm fetches as the poll catalogues new steps of the newest run, for the parameters and levels position queries read in the last 24 hours, and pre-warmed messages a request then reads from the message cache, each counted at its first read. Bursts follow model runs. Fetched far above read means the pre-warm fetches what nobody asks for.

spec.title: GRIB pre-warm bytes
spec.description: Bytes per second the GRIB pre-warm fetches into the message cache. Each run takes at most a quarter of the source's message_cache_mb, and nothing of a parameter level whose messages of the run the cache cannot hold.

spec.title: GRIB pre-warmed messages read, last 24 h
spec.description: Share of the messages the GRIB pre-warm fetched over the last 24 hours that a request then read. Low means the parameters read once a day are not the ones read now; the pre-warm costs storage reads for them.

spec.expr: sum by (collection) (increase(grib_prewarm_hits_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[24h])) / sum by (collection) (increase(grib_prewarm_gets_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[24h]))

spec.title: GRIB map read-ahead: messages fetched and read
spec.description: Messages per second the GRIB map read-ahead fetches after a WMS, Maps or Tiles render draws a step, the messages it would draw at the run's next steps, and read-ahead messages a request then reads, each counted at its first read, a request that joined the fetch included. Bursts follow animations over a cold run. Fetched far above read means clients do not step forward through the run: the read-ahead fetches frames nobody draws.

spec.title: GRIB map read-ahead bytes
spec.description: Bytes per second the GRIB map read-ahead fetches into the message cache. Each run takes at most a quarter of the source's message_cache_mb, a share of its own beside the pre-warm's, with two GETs in flight shared with the pre-warm, and nothing of a parameter whose next steps the cache cannot hold together.

spec.title: GRIB read-ahead messages read, last 24 h
spec.description: Share of the messages the GRIB map read-ahead fetched over the last 24 hours that a request then read. Low means clients jump between steps or runs rather than step forward, and the read-ahead costs storage reads for frames nobody draws; read_ahead = 0 turns it off for a source.

spec.expr: sum by (collection) (increase(grib_read_ahead_hits_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[24h])) / sum by (collection) (increase(grib_read_ahead_gets_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[24h]))

spec.title: Icechunk storage requests
spec.description: Storage requests per second each Icechunk repository issues: every part of a ranged read, listings, and Icechunk's own retries; retries inside the HTTP client are not counted. A catalog build after a snapshot change reads the new snapshot, the manifests and the default run's shard indexes; after that a cold position read is one request per inner chunk that misses the payload cache. Requests that do not follow traffic or snapshot changes point at retries.

spec.title: Icechunk storage bytes
spec.description: Bytes per second the bodies of each Icechunk repository's storage reads yield: snapshots, manifests, shard indexes, and chunk ranges that missed the payload cache (zarr_icechunk_payload_cache). Divided by the requests beside it, this is the mean size of a read.

spec.title: Demand by cache
spec.description: Each cache's demand over its own configured capacity (cache_demand_ratio): what the engines say a cache must hold for their data, a process-wide cache's summed over its collections, a per-collection cache's its collection's. Above 1, the red line, a cache is below its demand, and the server logged one WARN naming the inputs and the size to set. A disabled cache has no series. The PVOL pixel cache's demand is a floor, twice the pre-warm set: requests need more. /admin/cache-plan lists each demand's inputs and the suggested size; the Cache plan table has the demand in bytes.

spec.title: Memory plan
spec.description: The memory the plan fits every cache and budget into (memory_plan_total_bytes: [memory] total_mb, else 80 % of a cgroup limit, else the smaller of half of MemTotal and 80 % of MemAvailable at boot), what the caches share of it after the reserves (memory_plan_pool_bytes: memory outside the caches, the render budget, the largest read budget and allocator slack), and how much more it needs with the pins kept and every other cache and budget at its floor (memory_plan_shortfall_bytes, red above 0). Fitted at boot and at each reload. A report: no size is changed. The server logs the plan with one WARN when it cuts a cache below its configured size; the Cache plan table has each planned size.

spec.title: Plan against memory
spec.description: Caches and budgets summed, as the memory plan sizes them (cache_planned_bytes) and as configured (memory_capacity_total_bytes), against the plan's total and cache pool, and RSS (Linux only). Sizes are ceilings: a cache allocates as it fills, so either sum can lie above the total while RSS stays below it. A step is a restart or reload that planned again.

spec.title: Data age vs expected interval
spec.description: Each collection's data age next to the interval its data arrives at (collection_expected_interval_seconds: the median spacing of its newest timesteps or runs, or its expected_interval), the age at which the CollectionStale alert's condition holds (3 intervals, and at least an interval + 15 min) and the age over it. Red from 100 %: the alert fires once that has held for 10 min. A collection with no interval (one timestep and no expected_interval) shows – and is never stale.

spec.expr: max by (collection) ((3 * collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} > collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900) or (collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900))

max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) / max by (collection) ((3 * collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} > collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900) or (collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900))

spec.title: Data age over stale threshold
spec.description: Each collection's data age over the age at which the CollectionStale alert's condition holds: 3 times its expected interval, and at least the interval + 15 min. A sawtooth below the red line is normal; above it for 10 min the alert fires. Collections without an expected interval have no line. Click a series to filter the dashboard to it.

spec.expr: max by (collection) (collection_data_age_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}) / max by (collection) ((3 * collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} > collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900) or (collection_expected_interval_seconds{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"} + 900))

spec.title: WMS error tiles
spec.description: WMS GetMaps answered with the red error tile per second, by collection and reason (wms_error_tiles_total). They are HTTP 200, so the status code panels never count them. reason: not_found = the data the request named was gone, invalid_request = the engine refused the request (such as a source read over its pixel cap), storage = a source read failed, internal = any other. The server log has each render error.

spec.title: WMS error-tile ratio by collection
spec.description: The share of each collection's GetMap responses that are the red error tile: error tiles over error tiles plus served renders (render_duration_seconds, api wms). The red line is the WmsErrorTiles alert's 5 %, which fires once it has held for 10 min.

spec.expr: sum by (collection) (rate(wms_error_tiles_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (collection) (rate(wms_error_tiles_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[$__rate_interval])) + (sum by (collection) (rate(render_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", api="wms", collection=~"$collection"}[$__rate_interval])) or sum by (collection) (rate(wms_error_tiles_total{job=~"$job", collection=~"$collection"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0))
